text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3% today after climbing sharply over the prior three trading days, erasing most of those gains. The stock had surged to $414.65 on November 13th—likely on tightness in diesel and heating oil markets, given the news that heating oil prices are up 59% year-over-year—but that bullish setup weakened when the International Energy Agency reported on November 13th that Russian crude production is rebounding and global oil markets are moving back into surplus. With crude supply no longer constrained and refineries already running at 95.2% capacity, the case for outsize refining profits has cooled.

The broader headwind is straightforward: rising energy costs are starting to squeeze demand. Heating oil prices spiking 59% are "crushing folks," according to reporting on household budgets, and shipping executives are signaling retailers are pulling back on holiday inventory orders due to transportation cost pressure. For a refiner, rising input costs (crude) paired with weakening demand signals (cautious holiday restocking, expensive heating oil crimping consumer budgets) is a mix that tends to compress margins.
